transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-29
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 min
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Karen Liu (Entwood - Head of Security), Marco Reyes (Entwood - Platform Lead), Priya Nair (Entwood - Compliance)

Auto-generated summary (may be noisy):
- Entwood is evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private for customer-facing recommendation engine and internal agent; strongest concerns are SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs retention, and KMS integration.
- They want SOC2 artifacts, encryption at rest details and a pilot to run request patterns.
- Next steps: send SOC2, SAML guide, schedule pilot, provide pricing matrix.

Topics covered:
- SOC2/state of certifications
- SSO/SAML integration and IdP flows
- RBAC scoping for cross-team access
- Audit log granularity and retention options
- Encryption: KMS/HSM BYOK vs Redwood-managed keys
- Data residency and retention/erase SLA
- Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs for latency and isolation

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining on a Thursday afternoon, um i'm Alex from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account. Samir my solutions engineer is here.
[00:08] Karen Liu: hi all, thanks, i'm Karen, head of security at Entwood. we pulled Marco and Priya in because they'll own the platform and compliance pieces.
[00:15] Marco Reyes: morning — afternoon — yeah thanks for doing this.
[00:19] Samir Patel: great; quick agenda, if that's ok: SOC2 and compliance artifacts, how SSO/SAML would plug in, RBAC model we support, audit logging options and KMS/encryption. we'll leave time for Q's and next steps. sound good?
[00:31] Priya Nair: sounds good.
[00:35] Karen Liu: yeah go ahead. we're most concerned about auditability and ability to demonstrate controls to auditors — and also how keys are managed if we need BYOK.

[03:02] Samir Patel: on SOC 2 — Redwood has SOC 2 Type II for our hosted offering; for Dedicated the control plane is still Redwood-managed unless you take Private. we can produce the SOC2 report and a gap memo for Dedicated/private differences. i'll attach the report after.
[03:25] Karen Liu: so for Dedicated, do we get the same control coverage or are there carve-outs? auditor will ask.
[03:33] Samir Patel: there are a couple of carve-outs around physical datacenter controls and some network segmentation that's customer-managed for Private. Dedicated is still covered broadly but we provide a supplements doc that lists what you own vs Redwood.
[04:10] Marco Reyes: ok yeah that helps. what about pen test evidence and recent attestation dates?
[04:18] Alex Chen: pen test summary and dates included in the SOC2 pack — we'll share the redacted reports.

[06:00] Priya Nair: question on SSO — we're on Okta as IdP; we use SAML and SCIM for user sync. how do you support that for admin access and service accounts?
[06:18] Samir Patel: good Q. we support SAML 2.0 for console and API SSO for login flows, and SCIM for provisioning. service-to-service keys are managed via our RBAC and service roles; for programmatic calls you can create fine-grained API keys with scopes and expiration.
[06:41] Karen Liu: when you say SAML 2.0, do you mean standard metadata exchange? we need signed assertions and SP-initiated flows.
[06:52] Samir Patel: yes, we do SP-initiated and IdP-initiated, require signed assertions — the metadata exchange is standard. sometimes the speech-to-text mislabels SAML as 'Samuel' in notes, sorry if that shows up in docs.

[09:05] Marco Reyes: RBAC — we need to map our org roles: data scientists, platform, SRE, product. can we mirror groups from Okta and then map roles in Redwood?
[09:18] Samir Patel: absolutely. we support group-sync via SCIM; you can map Okta groups to Redwood roles. we have built-in roles (admin, operator, developer, viewer) and custom roles for granular permissions — e.g., allow-only-embed, no-export.
[09:38] Karen Liu: can we restrict access so only a tiny set can view raw transcripts and export logs? that's important for PHI in a few flows.
[09:49] Alex Chen: yes, RBAC can be scoped to redact or disallow transcript exports. redaction is also possible at ingestion via filters, but retention and export controls are handled by role policies.

[12:10] Priya Nair: audit logs — what do they capture? we need user actions, API calls, token-level usage and changes to config and keys. retention must be at least 3 years for our auditors.
[12:28] Samir Patel: our audit logs capture auth events, admin actions (role grants, policy changes), API calls (request id, model, latency, truncated token counts), and system events. we can stream logs to your SIEM (S3/CloudWatch/GCS/HTTPS webhook). default retention in hosted is 90 days but for Dedicated/Private we can configure longer retention; we'll provide a matrix of options and costs.
[12:55] Marco Reyes: streaming is important. can we get the event schema? we want to map fields into Splunk.
[13:04] Samir Patel: yes — we'll share the event schema and a sample week of anonymized logs. note that some fields will be redacted by default in hosted for PII.

[15:40] Karen Liu: KMS — we want BYOK and HSM backed keys, with key rotation policies. can Redwood integrate with our AWS KMS or do you require Redwood-managed keys?
[15:54] Samir Patel: for Private and Dedicated you can bring your own keys (BYOK) via AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or our HSM partner. Hosted supports customer-managed keys via cloud KMS in certain regions — we'll list region limitations. rotation and audit logs are surfaced. for BYOK you keep key material ownership but Redwood uses a wrapped key approach for runtime encryption.
[16:22] Priya Nair: any SLA for key deletion on termination? we need confirmable erase.
[16:30] Alex Chen: yes we have documented key deletion flows; for Private you control keys entirely. for Dedicated/hosted we provide a key wipe procedure with attestation within X days — we'll include the process doc.

[19:05] Marco Reyes: data residency — do you host in eu-west and us-west? we may need EU-only for EU customers.
[19:12] Samir Patel: we have region control. Hosted lets you pin region per org; Dedicated can be deployed in the region of your choice, and Private is fully in your VPC/on-prem. we can discuss sub-region constraints and data egress controls.

[21:55] Karen Liu: retention & erase — if a user requests deletion, can you delete all personally identifying content from logs and model cache? what about KV cache?
[22:12] Samir Patel: we support data deletion requests. for model KV cache, we have TTL and purge APIs; for Hosted there are default caching rules but we can configure per-workload for the pilot. we will detail exactly what gets purged and what remains for audit trail.

[24:40] Marco Reyes: performance vs retention question — if we lengthen logs retention and keep richer logs, any impact on latency or cost?
[24:53] Samir Patel: audit logs are off-path for inference and usually don't affect inference latency; the cost impact is on storage and ingest pipeline. caching/kv settings influence token costs and latency. more aggressive caching reduces token cost but retains more state — which ties into your retention requirements.

[27:30] Priya Nair: can we run a pilot with PII redaction enabled and see how it impacts accuracy?
[27:38] Samir Patel: yes, we can enable redaction at ingestion for the pilot, and Samir will run a controlled set with your test prompts. we'll collect quality metrics.

[30:05] Alex Chen: competitors — just to be transparent, who else are you evaluating?
[30:12] Karen Liu: few vendors; BigCloud AI for hosted convenience, and AuroraServe for an on-premish model. privacy and cost are the main axes.

[32:20] Marco Reyes: question about network isolation — for Dedicated is there a VPC peering option or do we rely on private endpoints?
[32:33] Samir Patel: Dedicated uses private endpoints and can be peered into your VPC, and you can restrict egress. Private is full VPC deployment with customer-managed networking. we'll send diagrams.

[35:05] Priya Nair: on legal — how does logging retention interplay with e-discovery and legal holds?
[35:18] Alex Chen: good question — we support hold flags to prevent auto-deletion; retention policies can be tailored and holds can be applied to specific accounts or tenant IDs. you'll need a runbook for retention exceptions; we'll provide sample runbook.

[37:40] Karen Liu: for auditors we need to show change history for RBAC and who elevated privileges. is that included in audit logs?
[37:50] Samir Patel: yes, admin events include before/after snapshots for role changes and the user who performed the action. we can keep the diffs for your retention period.

[40:10] Marco Reyes: cost question — how much incremental cost to push retention from 90 days to 3 years?
[40:22] Alex Chen: depends on log volume — we'll provide a price estimate based on sample ingest rates you provide. rough ballpark in our pricing sheet is X per GB-month for long-term retention. i'll include the calculator.

[42:05] Priya Nair: ok next steps recap please.
[42:12] Alex Chen: sure. Samir will send the SOC2 and pen test summary, event schema + sample logs, and SAML/SCIM integration guide. i'll send pricing matrix and Dedicated vs Private decision doc. we'll stand up a Dedicated demo cluster for a benchmark and schedule pilot kickoff week of Aug 3.
[42:31] Karen Liu: that works. can you mark the items in CRM?
[42:36] Alex Chen: will do — CRM id is CRM-ENT-8492.

[44:00] Marco Reyes: one last nit — can we get a sample SLA for key deletion? auditors will ask timeline.
[44:09] Samir Patel: yes we'll include deletion attestation and timeline, typically 30 days with a quicker process for Private.

[46:00] Alex Chen: perfect. thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the artifacts.
[46:06] Karen Liu: thank you.
[46:09] Priya Nair: thanks all.
[46:12] Marco Reyes: bye.

End of recording.
